sources.title: U.S. Data Centers Tracker
sources.use: Facility locations, project status, reported MW, operators, power-source labels, acreage, direct community-pushback flags, and timeline fields.
sources.notes: Uses Data_Centers_Database_102726.xlsx, sheet DB_Output_V2. Missing capacity remains unknown. Reported or expected online years and inventory-added dates are not a verified opening history. FracTracker’s source records contain the underlying facility references.

reuse.notes: FracTracker permits downloading and sharing this tracker for noncommercial use with credit. Public access is not an unrestricted open-data license.

sources.title: eGRID 2024 power plants
sources.use: Plant locations, fuel categories, nameplate capacity, generation, capacity factors, and nearby generation totals.
sources.notes: The dashboard uses a provisional development build, not a final eGRID release. The recorded development commit is linked below. Nearby generation does not establish supply to a data center.

reuse.notes: EPA states that eGRID data are public domain and may be used commercially or noncommercially. The recorded development repository also carries an MIT software license. This dashboard uses provisional output; retain the EPA credit and snapshot caveat.

sources.title: eGRID subregion boundaries
sources.use: Facility eGRID subregion assignments and regional grid context.
sources.notes: Boundary vintage differs from the 2024 power-plant data. Geographic assignment does not verify a physical grid connection.

reuse.notes: EPA’s default data policy places EPA-produced data in the U.S. public domain unless a dataset says otherwise. Keep attribution and the boundary-vintage caveat.

sources.title: Electric Retail Service Territories
sources.use: Candidate electric utility territories for facility locations.
sources.notes: Overlapping territories remain ambiguous. A geographic match is not confirmation of the serving utility. The original ArcGIS item and service identify the downloaded dataset; current contents may differ from the saved snapshot.

reuse.status: Public use: no use restrictions in metadata
reuse.notes: The saved HIFLD item metadata states “None (Public Use)” and credits Oak Ridge National Laboratory and U.S. DOE CESER. Read its geographic and accuracy limitations.

sources.title: EIA-861 utility and operational data
sources.vintage: 2024 Utility, Operational, and Balancing Authority files
sources.use: Utility context and reported facility MW relative to a candidate utility’s peak demand.
sources.notes: Utility-relative scale uses an unverified spatial utility candidate. It is not available grid capacity or a deliverability assessment.

reuse.notes: EIA permits reuse and redistribution of its data and requests acknowledgement. The policy excludes any separately identified third-party copyrighted material.

sources.title: State electricity prices
sources.publisher: U.S. EIA; prepared by Dynamical Systems Laboratory
sources.use: State industrial electricity prices, companion total-sector prices, and historical variance in the national and U.S. hex views.
sources.notes: Uses eia861_state_prices_real_2020_with_volatility.csv from the linked research repository. Coverage is the contiguous 48 states. State averages are not a facility tariff or negotiated rate.

reuse.status: Mixed: EIA public domain; prepared-file license unverified
reuse.notes: EIA permits reuse of its original data. No repository-wide license was found for the prepared research CSV or preparation code; public GitHub access alone does not establish a license for those contributions.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U)
sources.vintage: Historical CPI-U workbook, August 2025 edition; 2020 price base
sources.use: Inflation-adjusted companion values in the prepared electricity-price series.
sources.notes: The dashboard’s map uses nominal cents per kWh. CPI-adjusted companion values are part of its published price data.

reuse.notes: BLS identifies its published statistical material as public domain and requests citation. This covers the CPI input, not a separate license for third-party price-preparation code.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap power infrastructure
sources.use: Transmission-line overlays and line length, plus nearest-line and nearest-substation context.
sources.notes: The national overlay includes lines tagged 200 kV or higher. Contributor coverage and voltage tags vary. Proximity does not establish connection or spare capacity. © OpenStreetMap contributors; ODbL.

reuse.notes: Credit OpenStreetMap contributors and link the license. The ODbL includes share-alike requirements for adapted databases; public availability alone is not the full set of reuse conditions.

sources.title: Queued Up interconnection data
sources.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and GridTracker
sources.use: County-level active generation queue MW and contextual queue pressure.
sources.notes: Positive reported capacity components are aggregated by county. These are generation interconnection requests, not data-center load requests or guaranteed future power supply.

reuse.notes: The Queued Up download page identifies CC BY 4.0 and requires credit to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and GridTracker. The dashboard aggregates project records to county totals.

sources.title: AWARE water-scarcity factors
sources.publisher: WULCA; county file distributed by Dynamical Systems Laboratory
sources.vintage: Prepared county annual-average factors; context reviewed 8 October 2026
sources.use: Water-scarcity classes and comparison variables across facility, hexagon, and Virginia county views.
sources.notes: Uses AWARE_US_CF.csv. The exact AWARE release is not recorded in the dashboard metadata; do not assume it is the latest AWARE2.0 release. County factors do not measure facility water use or water rights.

reuse.status: Unverified for the exact prepared snapshot
reuse.notes: The exact AWARE release and license of AWARE_US_CF.csv were not recorded. The distribution repository has no repository-wide license. A license for a newer WULCA release cannot establish permission for this saved file.

sources.title: County-level water-use estimates
sources.use: Total county water withdrawal in the hexagon and Virginia county explorers.
sources.notes: Historical withdrawals are separate from water scarcity and do not establish present supply headroom or a specific data center’s consumption.

reuse.notes: USGS-produced data are in the U.S. public domain; keep the dataset citation. Separately credited third-party material may have different rights.

sources.title: National Risk Index
sources.publisher: Federal Emergency Management Agency; county file distributed by Dynamical Systems Laboratory
sources.vintage: Prepared county table; context reviewed 8 October 2026
sources.use: Overall risk and drought, heat-wave, riverine-flood, and wildfire scores or ratings.
sources.notes: Uses NRI_Table_Counties.csv. Exact NRI release is not recorded in the dashboard metadata. County screening measures are not parcel-level hazard determinations.

reuse.status: Unverified for the exact prepared snapshot
reuse.notes: The source program is FEMA, but the exact release and reuse terms of the prepared NRI_Table_Counties.csv were not preserved. The research repository has no repository-wide license, so this audit does not certify the prepared copy as openly licensed.

sources.title: County Business Patterns
sources.use: County counts of data-processing, hosting, and related-services establishments.
sources.notes: Establishments are a broader business measure and should not be read as the dashboard’s physical data-center count.

reuse.status: Federal statistical data; Census use conditions
reuse.notes: Published Census statistics are federal data. Census API terms permit applications and analysis, prohibit respondent identification, and specify source/nonendorsement notices. This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.

sources.title: Census boundaries and Gazetteer locations
sources.vintage: 2023 state boundaries; 2024 county boundaries; 2026 Gazetteer files; Census TIGERweb fallback point
sources.use: State outlines, county assignments, area-based measures, Virginia’s 133 counties and independent cities, and the boundary framework for derived hexagons. Gazetteer internal points locate local-action jurisdictions.
sources.notes: The 50 km and 100 km hexagon grids are project-generated in an equal-area projection. Gazetteer points represent jurisdictions, not data-center sites. County and state attributes assigned to cells remain contextual geographic measures. The local-action preparation also uses a Census TIGERweb federal-reservation internal point for Eastern Cherokee Reservation (code 0990). The exact service version was not saved.

reuse.notes: The saved 2024 TIGER/Line metadata says the files are not copyrighted and permits use with Census acknowledgement. The Gazetteer and TIGERweb inputs are Census geographic data; geographic boundaries are not legal land descriptions.

sources.title: Subsidizing Servers: state tax incentives
sources.use: Dedicated data-center incentives, electricity-tax treatment, and other state-policy context.
sources.notes: A state incentive flag does not establish project eligibility, receipt, or the value of an award.

reuse.notes: NCSL’s general terms do not provide an open-data license. They allow personal viewing/printing and require permission for reproduction or redistribution unless specifically authorized. This source attribution does not itself establish permission for a derivative compilation.

sources.title: Which States Are Banning Data Centers?
sources.use: State moratorium tracker counts and statuses.
sources.notes: Tracked proposals include introduced, failed, vetoed, and other statuses. A tracker entry does not mean a ban is in force.

reuse.notes: NCSL’s general terms do not provide an open-data license. They allow personal viewing/printing and require permission for reproduction or redistribution unless specifically authorized. This source attribution does not itself establish permission for a derivative compilation.

sources.title: State data-center legislation records
sources.publisher: Project compilation based principally on LegiScan legislative records
sources.use: State bill counts, topic filters, source status, and bill-detail links.
sources.notes: The original workbook’s methodology identifies LegiScan metadata, summaries, and bill texts as its principal inputs. The published dashboard retains 547 state bill records from the 549-row workbook, omitting two federal records. The register below reproduces every published record and its source URL. Categories may overlap; bill counts do not measure regulatory stringency. Follow the individual source for subsequent actions.

reuse.notes: No explicit open license was recorded in the source workbook. All 544 distinct links in the 547-record register point to LegiScan. Bill texts, provider metadata, and the project’s classifications are distinct contributions; public access to a bill does not establish an open license for the whole compilation.

sources.title: U.S. Datacenter Fights event database
sources.publisher: Cam Acosta, George Ingebretsen, and community contributors
sources.use: County and state opposition-event counts and contextual tracker matches.
sources.notes: This opposition-event database is not a representative opinion survey. No tracker match means unknown. Direct facility-pushback flags originate in the FracTracker inventory. This dashboard derives county and state summaries from the event database.

reuse.status: Open data: CC BY 4.0; code: MIT
reuse.notes: The repository explicitly distinguishes CC BY 4.0 data from MIT code. Credit Cam Acosta and George Ingebretsen, link the license, and identify aggregations or other changes.

sources.title: Local bans, moratoriums, and protective ordinances
sources.vintage: Prepared local-action inventory; context reviewed 8 October 2026
sources.use: Local-action counts and county context in the national, hexagon, and Virginia views.
sources.notes: Uses the project’s geocoded FracTracker local-action workbook. A county action count does not establish that an action applies to a particular facility.

reuse.status: Unverified workbook; provider has noncommercial terms
reuse.notes: FracTracker’s tracker page permits noncommercial sharing with credit. The exact local-action workbook did not carry a separately recorded license, so unrestricted reuse of that workbook is not verified.

sources.title: 2024 Precinct-Level Election Results
sources.use: Presidential vote margins and precinct maps loaded by state in the national view.
sources.notes: © The New York Times Company. Precinct coverage and boundary quality vary. The dashboard loads precinct data from NYT and stores only a coverage manifest. Voting is political context, not evidence of views about data centers.

links.label: Checked state feed URLs and link-audit results

reuse.notes: The repository uses the NYT Computational Use of Data Agreement, Version 1.0 – Non-Commercial. It requires attribution and limits computational use, results, and redistribution, with a specified editorial exception. This is not an unrestricted open-data license.

sources.title: 2024 Pres by CD
sources.publisher: Drew Savicki and contributing election-data researchers
sources.use: Harris, Trump, and all-candidate presidential vote totals by congressional district.
sources.notes: This compiled sheet combines state election sources and contributed calculations. Ten rows have one-vote rounding differences. Margins use all presidential votes as the denominator.

reuse.status: Unverified: no explicit open license found
reuse.notes: The public spreadsheet and its contributor/source credits do not establish an open license for the compiled sheet. Preserve attribution; permission for unrestricted reuse remains unverified.

sources.title: 2026 U.S. House election results
sources.use: Democratic, Republican, and all-candidate House votes, race calls, and reporting estimates.
sources.notes: This snapshot is not live or certified. Four districts have no reported vote totals. Margins use all reported candidate votes; voting does not measure attitudes toward data centers.

reuse.status: Reuse allowed with attribution: civicAPI terms
reuse.notes: civicAPI’s FAQ permits personal, noncommercial, and commercial data use and requires noncommercial/commercial users to credit civicAPI. Polling Desk says underlying data retain their original licenses; its own writing, design, and charts are separately protected. This is a provider use statement, not a blanket software license.

sources.title: Congressional district boundaries
sources.use: District geometry and facility-to-district assignments for both congressional voting layers.
sources.notes: The presidential layer uses 119th Congress boundaries. The 2026 House layer uses 120th Congress boundaries for 49 states and the unchanged 119th Congress Missouri plan. Four facility points are unassigned in the presidential layer and two in the 2026 House layer.

reuse.notes: TIGER/Line metadata permits reuse with Census acknowledgement and says the shapefiles are not copyrighted. Boundaries are statistical products, not legal land descriptions.
